summary: Built on the BEAM virtual machine: millions of isolated processes, supervision trees, and nine-nines uptime fault tolerance.

rows.means: defines a namespace of related functions
rows.consequence: In Elixir, all functions reside inside modules; functions are identified by name and arity (e.g. String.length/1).

rows.means: passes the result of the left expression as the first argument to the right
rows.consequence: Turns nested function calls inside out: data |> validate() |> transform() |> save() reads cleanly top-to-bottom.

rows.means: pattern matches data structures rather than simple assignment
rows.consequence: {:ok, result} = fetch_user(id) asserts that the call succeeded and binds result; crashes cleanly if {:error, _} is returned.

rows.means: immutable identifier whose name is its own value
rows.consequence: Atoms like :ok, :error, :nil are stored in an internal atom table; fast O(1) comparison by memory pointer.

rows.means: contiguous fixed-size group / singly linked list for iteration
rows.consequence: Tuples are ideal for pattern-matching return values; lists support fast [head | tail] deconstruction.
Maps allow any key type. Updates (%{ map | key: "new" }) create efficient structural-sharing copies.

rows.means: starts a lightweight process belonging to the runtime
rows.consequence: These are not operating system threads: they are created and scheduled by the runtime, start with a very small amount of memory, and are isolated from one another, which is why a program can hold hundreds of thousands of them and why one dying harms nothing else.

rows.code: send(pid, msg) and receive do msg -> ... end
rows.means: asynchronous message passing between isolated processes
rows.consequence: Processes have private heaps and mailboxes. If a process crashes, it cannot corrupt memory in any other process.

rows.means: a standard behaviour for a stateful server process
rows.consequence: Standardises the callbacks — init, handle_call, handle_cast, handle_info — so that every stateful process in a system is started, called and supervised the same way.

rows.means: monitors child processes and restarts them on failure
rows.consequence: Instead of defensive code trying to handle every rare corrupt state, crashed processes are simply restarted from clean initial state.

rows.means: functional transformations over collections and streams
rows.consequence: The eager versions build the whole collection at each step; the lazy module defers the work so a large source is walked once rather than copied repeatedly.
